messages:
chris: FYI ACME (tenant=acme-corp) opened a support ticket: widespread 401s after an API key rotation this morning. They say backend calls to /v1/generate return 401 invalid_api_key, but other admin API calls succeed. Logs attached.

maya: Do they have an example request/response body? Is it all pods or a subset?

chris: Pasted sample from their app log:
```json
{"time":"2026-03-16T09:12:03Z","status":401,"error":"invalid_api_key","hint":"key revoked or scope mismatch","request":{"path":"/v1/generate","method":"POST","headers":{"authorization":"Bearer sk_live_OLDKEY..."}}}
```

ryan: Sounds like some processes are still using the old key. Are they using env vars or a file-based secret from a sidecar? We saw stale sidecar caches cause similar symptoms.

chris: They say they rotate keys via our UI, then kubernetes rolling update. Their stack uses a small secret-sync sidecar that writes to /etc/secrets/apikey and the app reads that file. They ran `kubectl rollout restart deployment/foo` but ~30% of pods still returned old key. I pulled one pod and ran: 
```
# kubectl exec -it pod-123 -- cat /etc/secrets/apikey
sk_live_OLDKEY...
# kubectl exec -it pod-456 -- cat /etc/secrets/apikey
sk_live_NEWKEY...
```

maya: If the sidecar writes atomically, processes that keep the file open will still read the old content from their file descriptor. Ask them to check if the app keeps the file open and doesn't re-open on read. Also check if they rely on long-lived connection pools that cache headers.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-4723 - "acme-corp 401s after key rotation". Priority: P2. Assignee: ryan.

ryan: Repro suggestion for customer: 1) rotate a test key 2) don't restart app process, only restart sidecar so file changes but app process keeps fd open 3) send request -> should get 401 if app didn't re-open file. For diagnostics ask them to run inside a pod: `lsof -p $(pidof app) | grep apikey` and `ls -l /proc/$(pidof app)/fd | grep apikey` to see if fd points to the old inode.

chris: Sent those steps. Customer tried them and confirmed the app process had the file open to an older inode — sidecar updates create a new file instead of updating in place. They did `stat /etc/secrets/apikey` on pods: some had mtime from new rotation, others old.

maya: Short-term fix: restart the application process inside affected pods so it re-reads the file. If they're on a Deployment, `kubectl rollout restart` should replace pods; if not, `pkill -HUP app` or `systemctl restart` equivalent. For client SDKs, also clear any cached tokens.

ryan: Long-term guidance: make the secret-sync write atomically (write to tmp + mv) and optionally keep the same inode (truncate+write) if the app relies on inode. Better: have the app watch file changes or fetch secrets via a local token server instead of direct file reads. We'll also add a note to docs about sidecar atomicity.

chris: Customer restarted the app processes and ~80% of requests recovered. They still report mobile clients getting 401s intermittently — likely client-side cached keys or CDN edge caching auth headers.

maya: For mobile clients: ask them to flush any client-side key cache and invalidate sessions. Also check if their edge/gateway caches are incorrectly configured to cache responses that include auth headers. Suggest verifying caching rules and invalidating the CDN.

ryan: I'm going to check our revocation propagation logs for tenant acme-corp to ensure our revocation event reached all edge nodes at rotation time. If propagation lag exists, we'll follow up and patch.

chris: Thanks — I updated the ticket with the workaround (restart app processes, invalidate client caches) and the recommended long-term fixes. Customer is scheduling an afternoon maintenance window to do a full pod restart and CDN invalidation.

maya: Nice. If you need SRE help during their maintenance window ping `#oncall-sre`. Also adding a short KB entry for common causes of post-rotation 401s (sidecar file fd open, connection pool reuse, client caches).

ryan: Assigned follow-up tasks: check edge propagation timeline, draft KB, and file a small infra PR to add inode-preserving write mode to our reference secret-syncer.

chris: Marking this thread resolved for now — will re-open if customer sees >5% error rate after full restart. :thumbsup:
